title: Content Candidate
description: Raw material handed to a separate downstream Content Agent. The absolute rule of this OS is enforced here by structure: THE JOURNAL AGENT NEVER WRITES POSTS. There is no field in this file for a post, a caption, a hook, a headline, a thread, a script, an angle or a draft of any kind, and additionalProperties is false at every level, so a written post cannot be stored even by a writer that wants to. Privacy defaults to the most protective value: a candidate is private until it has been positively cleared, a candidate marked private cannot carry a publish recommendation, and any third party present forces at least needs_review. Quotes must be verbatim (said_verbatim is const true), so a polished version of what the user meant cannot be recorded as something they said. Third parties are a single given name and nothing else.

moment.description: What happened, in one line, as a fact

raw_facts.description: The concrete details a writer would need: numbers, sequence, what was said, what broke, what it cost. No framing.

why_it_may_matter.description: The external reason someone unrelated to the user would care. Not because it was a big day.

evidence_available.description: What can be shown. An empty array is a valid and common answer, recorded rather than glossed.

possible_themes.description: Themes only. Not angles, not hooks, not titles.

third_party_present.description: True whenever anyone but the user appears in the material. It forces at least needs_review.

quotable_raw_thoughts.description: Things the user actually said tonight, verbatim, in the language they said them in. Never manufactured, never tightened.

visual_assets.description: Only what the user mentioned already exists. MIRROR never assigns a shoot.

recommendation_reason.description: One sentence. Why this verdict and not the neighbouring one.

user_flagged_off_the_record.description: The user asked for it to stay out. Absolute, requires no reason, and forces private.

allOf.description: A private candidate cannot carry a publish recommendation. This is the core boundary of the content handoff.
Anyone but the user in the material means a human reviews it, whatever the user feels about it tonight.
A named person is a third party present. The two cannot disagree.

privacy.description: Closed by design. public_safe means nothing here identifies or exposes anyone but the user. needs_review means a human decides before anything goes out. private means not publishable at any distance, and is the default a candidate keeps until it is positively cleared.

recommendation.description: no_need_to_publish is the most common correct answer and is never a shortfall. A handoff that reports strong signal every night has started performing.

person_ref.description: The ONLY permitted representation of a third party. There is no field for a surname, an employer, an address, a phone number, an email, a handle, a profile link or a photo.

first_name.description: A single given name or an initial. The pattern rejects whitespace, digits and punctuation, so a full name, an email or a handle cannot be written here.

quote.description: Exactly as said, in the language it was said in

said_verbatim.description: Const true by design. A tidied or invented line cannot be stored as something the user said.

exists.description: Only evidence that already exists is listed. Nothing here is a request to go and produce it.

mentioned_by_user.description: Const true by design. MIRROR never assigns a shoot and never suggests capturing something tomorrow for content purposes.

where.description: Where the user said it is, if they said
